summary: ModelObservability console 403 after Okta SCIM group update — role claim missing
description:
Issue summary:
A handful of platform engineers (team: model-platform) report being able to authenticate with Okta SSO but receiving HTTP 403 when opening the ModelObservability console. The browser shows a successful SAML/SSO redirect, but the console surface returns an RBAC denial.

Impact:
- 6 engineers (including two oncall) cannot access ModelObservability dashboards for alert triage.
- Potentially blocking incident response and model metric investigations.
- Scope currently appears limited to the ModelObservability console; other internal consoles (console.redwood.com) unaffected.

Environment:
- prod: us-east region
- Okta-managed SCIM provisioning for groups -> internal RBAC sync
- Affected users are on the dedicated model-platform Okta group: model-observability-admins (recently renamed in Okta to model-observability-admins_v2)

Steps to reproduce:
1) User logs into console via Okta SSO. 2) Okta redirects back to console with SAML assertion. 3) Console auth service calls internal /auth/claims endpoint to map SSO assertion to RBAC roles. 4) Auth service returns 200 but roles list is empty -> console shows 403.

Observed logs/snippets:
- Okta Provisioning event (2026-03-11 02:14:03 UTC): SCIM PATCH /Groups model-observability-admins_v2 -> 200 OK.
- Auth service trace (2026-03-12 08:05:12 UTC): requestId=8f3a7b; token_sub=U12345; okta_groups=["model-observability-admins_v2"] ; mapped_roles=[]
- RBAC sync job log (2026-03-12 03:00:00 UTC): "WARN: group attribute 'role' missing for group model-observability-admins_v2; skipping role assignment"

Initial hypothesis and findings:
- Suspect Okta-to-SCIM attribute mapping for 'role' claim was dropped when group rename (suffix _v2) was created. The RBAC sync expects a custom 'roles' attribute on the Okta Group object, and that attribute is only populated for groups created before the recent migration.
- Identity service accepts Okta groups but only assigns roles when the group-level custom attribute 'roles' is present. New groups created via the Okta automation lack that attribute due to a mapping condition in the provisioning policy.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Manual grant: Support manually granted 'observability.admin' in RBAC for 6 affected users via admin console at 2026-03-12 09:30 UTC to restore access.

Next steps and proposed remediation:
- Identity team to update Okta provisioning policy to include the custom group attribute 'roles' for new groups. (PR suggested: identity#4123)
- Backfill roles for groups created since 2026-03-01 via a one-off SCIM PATCH job.
- Add a defensive check in auth service: if group name matches known admin patterns (model-observability-*) and no group-level roles attribute present, emit audit alert and fallback to conservative role mapping only for emergency access (requires change and internal review).
- Add monitoring alert (Alert ID: MON-obs-rbac-empty-groups) when group mapped_roles == [] for users in console environment.

Acceptance criteria for closure:
- Okta provisioning policy updated and verified to populate 'roles' attribute for newly created/renamed groups.
- Backfill job completed and verified for model-observability groups.
- Affected users can authenticate and see expected admin UI without manual grants.
- Postmortem note added to Confluence and runbook updated with temporary mitigation steps.
